# CLAIMs with `role` `counter`

*Voices — Whose voice a CLAIM is in, within the record's own deliberation. Not whether the record believes it, which is the status: the two vary independently, and the mismatched pairs are the information (ADR-032).*

**Counter** — put forward on an opponent's behalf, at full strength — a steelman, or an objection anticipated as devil's advocate. A counter that goes Active means the record was persuaded, and the thesis it opposed needs revisiting.

The defeat condition fixes observables the thesis declines to fix, and tests them descriptively: [CLAIM-085](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-085.md)'s split of normative from descriptive, applied to the thesis rather than to model judges. It does not say the thesis is empty. | Active |
| [CLAIM-244](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-244.md) | The defeat tests take one holistic, task-free judgement of fidelity as ground truth, though the line's own theses say fidelity is task-relative, interpreter-relative and not a single ranking | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. A judge asked "how faithful?" or "the same kind?" supplies an unstated task and weighting, and is one interpreter. The theory's measure must then be fitted to that weighting, which is circular, or a mismatch blamed on the judges' task, which leaves nothing that defeats. It does not say the judgements are useless, only that the defeat conditions lack the task and receiver index the line's own theses say fidelity needs. [CLAIM-140](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md) is its neighbour: that one moves the criterion to the analyst, and neither says it is task-free. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-246](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-246.md) v2 | Sharing a kind is symmetric and blind to which work is the source, so the October thesis cannot say a translation is of its original, against the line's own directed, graded fidelity and identity through descent | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. [CLAIM-137](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-137.md) makes realizations one act by a shared invariant, "not resemblance to an original", and [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md)'s defeat condition tests judgements of shared kind. Sharing a kind is symmetric and says nothing of descent, so an utterance made independently of the source, of the same kind, scores as a translation does. The line's own theses make fidelity directed and graded ([CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md)) and identity partly a matter of transmission ([CLAIM-002](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-002.md)). The objection is open; it does not say descent must be part of fidelity, only that the kind criterion cannot state it. | Rejected |
| [CLAIM-248](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-248.md) v3 | A language model agreeing with humans in direction is weak evidence, because models are trained on human text about teasing and reproach and the founding stimuli are famous, and the language-model test bed's defeat condition fires only on a reversal | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. Agreement in direction is what a model trained on human descriptions of teasing and reproach would show anyway, and Villon, Henley and Hofstadter's Marot are likely in training data, so a model's "interpretation" of them may be recall. [ARG-008](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-008.md) and [CLAIM-085](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-085.md) already bound what model results show about human pragmatics. What is new is that [CLAIM-058](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-058.md)'s validity bar is too low, and the contamination point. Minor. | Active |
| [CLAIM-251](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-251.md) v2 | A change in which questions a receiver population can answer determinately is not by itself a change of cover in the sheaf sense: the cover belongs to the measurement scenario and the responses are an empirical model on it, so such a change is a change of empirical model, which can create or remove a gluing obstruction on a fixed cover but does not change what the cover is, and the operational notion needs its own name until a functorial link is shown | From the interlocutor's reading of PR [#121](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/121) and its reconciliation, relayed by the owner on 2026-10-12, on the open tension between [CLAIM-197](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-197.md) with [CASE-048](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-048.md) and the operational cover of [CLAIM-201](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-201.md). It keeps the empirical notion and denies it the sheaf-theoretic name. Open. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-253](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-253.md) v2 | The intertwining defects are defined on unobservable interpretive-state spaces, so they are not identified from judgement data, and the commutator identity bounds observed order effects only with a further, unstated readout-intertwining defect | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. The commutator identity is correct, but Φ, A and A′ act on interpretive states. [CLAIM-046](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-046.md) says hidden-state models that give identical observations can differ, and a worked case shows two such models with defects 0 and the largest possible, so the defect is not a function of the data. What is observed is responses, and the identity reaches the observed order effect only through a readout defect between outcome spaces, which no draft names. It is distinct from [CLAIM-011](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-011.md), which is about collapse: this is about identification. | Active |
| [CLAIM-254](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-254.md) | Read as the Saussure correction has it, the structuralist premise argues against transport: value is internal to one language state, so what can cross between languages is signification, the aspect the premise demotes | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. [CLAIM-072](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-072.md) corrects the manuscript's Saussure to value and says the correction "does not undercut the manuscript's use". But value is fixed inside one language state, so a change of language is a change of the system that fixes every value, and Saussure's own example has a term and its translation share a signification and differ in value. Value is also a fact of the language system, while the line's observables are facts of utterances in use. The objection is open. It does not say relational identity is false, only that Saussure, read correctly, does not support its transport. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-258](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-258.md) | Blackwell's order compares experiments about one parameter, so it does not reach the normal translation case: source and target readers decide about situations with changed coordinates, and where the state is common a translator with context knowledge yields a rendering that is not a garbling of the source, which the order typically leaves incomparable with it and about which the direction the manuscript uses is silent | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal and structure lenses); no turn of the exchange states it. [CLAIM-050](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md)'s comparison is over one state Z. Compensation ([CLAIM-091](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-091.md)) changes the social coordinates, so the target reader decides about a different situation. Where the situation is common, a translator who knows the context makes a rendering that depends on Z other than through the source, so it is not a garbling. Blackwell's order is still defined then, but typically leaves source and target incomparable, and the direction the manuscript uses says nothing. It does not say decision-relative fidelity is wrong. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-278](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-278.md) | An operator framework flexible enough to redescribe any dynamical process explains none of them until it forbids some outcome, and the shared-organization thesis has not yet said what it forbids | A7 §14's own first limitation, which the exchange granted and the record files as the standing objection to the explanatory thesis: "A sufficiently flexible operator framework could redescribe almost any dynamical process. The model must earn its value through restrictive assumptions, predictive compression, and intervention-sensitive predictions." It is [CLAIM-024](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-024.md)'s objection to the will paper, met by a second account. It is answered by a prediction the framework makes and its rivals do not. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-288](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-288.md) v2 | A simulation whose operators each maximize an objective the modeller fixed cannot show self-constitution, because the norms the organization appears to maintain are then the modeller's, not set by the organization itself | The record's objection, raised by no one in the exchange. A2 gives each operator an objective J_i, its evaluation of the collective decision, and A7 and A10 propose sufficiency tests run on such populations. Barandiaran, Di Paolo and Rohde hold that systems optimizing an externally fixed function are not models of agency ([NOTE-458](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-458.md), C5), and Di Paolo (2005) that a system's norms must be norms for the system. The objection undermines the evidence route; it does not refute the thesis. It is answered if the operators' objectives are themselves produced and revised by the organization. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-308](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-308.md) v2 | Where reuse cannot be forecast, recurrence weighted by reconstruction cost is the filing criterion, not only evidence for one: filing once the reconstruction already paid for equals the cost of filing is within twice the hindsight optimum on every sequence of uses, and no deterministic rule without foresight does better, under fixed known costs and with staleness left out | Filed at the owner's request, from the rent-or-buy result of Karlin et al. 1988 ([THEORY-348](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-348.md)) set against [CLAIM-303](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md)'s clause that recurrence is evidence of reuse, not the criterion. In [CLAIM-303](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md)'s own terms the break-even rule needs no forecast and is worst-case optimal; [ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)'s second-occurrence rule is that rule when filing costs about one reconstruction. It does not reach staleness, which the theorem forbids rather than prices, or drifting costs, and where reuse can be forecast an expected-reuse rule can do better, so [CLAIM-303](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md)'s criterion survives there. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-311](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-311.md) | A search cut off before an exhaustive pass can establish absence when the arrangement certifies that the unsearched remainder cannot hold the item: a sorted table answers non-membership in a logarithmic number of probes, and the Threshold Algorithm stops early with its answer proved, so absence needs a certificate about the remainder, not exhaustion; similarity search in high dimension is where no such certificate exists | Filed at the owner's request, from the database readings set against [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s asymmetry: presence by one find, absence "only by exhausting the collection". Sorted order and the Threshold Algorithm each establish absence from part of the collection, because the arrangement bounds what the rest can hold. That meets [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s own defeat condition, and the claim is conceded: [CLAIM-312](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-312.md) restates it. Where the arrangement gives no bound, as in similarity search in high dimension, [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s asymmetry stands. | Active |
| [CLAIM-313](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-313.md) v2 | A fixed number of bins realizes one partition only when each item is stored once: with copies, overlapping partitions coexist, as hashing-based similarity search stores each item in many partitions and pays for it in space, so sortings conflict as arrangements only under a one-copy constraint, which binds bricks but not index entries | Filed at the owner's request, from the readings on locality-sensitive hashing (Indyk and Motwani 1998; Andoni, Laarhoven, Razenshteyn and Waingarten 2017) set against [CLAIM-310](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md)'s premise that "a set of k bins realizes one partition of the collection at a time". That holds when each item is in one place. An index can hold many copies, and hashing-based similarity indexes do exactly that, trading the space of the copies against query time on an exact curve. It narrows [CLAIM-310](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md) to collections whose items cannot be copied, which includes the LEGO case; it does not touch the claim about descriptions. | Active |
| [CLAIM-314](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-314.md) | Reusing a filed argument has a recognition cost that a fixed per-use price leaves out: certifying that stored answers cover a new question is NP-complete even for conjunctive queries, grows with the number and size of the stored definitions rather than being a constant per item, and is undefined for an item filed without a statement of what it answers, so each filing raises the cost of later reuse and per-item break-even decisions are not independent | Filed at the owner's request, from the readings on answering queries using views (Levy, Mendelzon, Sagiv and Srivastava 1995; Chandra and Merlin 1977; Halevy 2001). [CLAIM-308](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-308.md)'s guarantee needs a fixed, known per-use cost c_a; recognizing that a stored answer covers a new question is a search whose cost depends on everything stored, so filing one item changes the price of using the others. It undermines the premise [CLAIM-308](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-308.md) states, not its arithmetic. The hardness is worst case and over short definitions, partial reuse is cheap, and nothing here is measured on the record. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-337](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-337.md) | Active inference already runs an internal loop: mental action selects among higher-level cognitive states and sets the precision of lower-level observations, structure learning reshapes the generative model without action, and a judgement is behaviour, so a judgement–observation loop may be action and perception one Markov blanket inward | The assistant's, A1 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, on active inference's behalf, strengthened at A4. Sandved-Smith et al. cast mental action as policy selection over higher-level cognitive states; Brouillet and Friston make felt fluency an inference about the precision of one's own processing; Smith et al. let a generative model grow its own structure by inference and learning alone. With Chalmers's point that judgements are behaviour, the owner's judgement is active inference's action relocated. What it does not reach: the diagram. A redescription with no action on the world concedes that action on the world is not part of the loop. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-339](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-339.md) | A judgement–observation loop cut off from action loses one route for evidence it did not select, and the free-energy principle's reason for minimizing surprise, that a persisting system must keep its states in bounds, needs action on the world, though a loop can confirm itself with action available too | The assistant's, A1 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, narrowed at A4. Friston et al. (2010) say active sampling is "mandated by ergodic arguments based on the very existence of adaptive agents", and the enactive account puts a system's own norms in its capacity to act against tendencies toward its viability boundary. Kübler and Birbaumer's extinction hypothesis is the empirical form. As first filed it said a loop without action has a self-confirming minimum. [NOTE-766](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-766.md) shows the minimum arises with action available, so the counter now claims only that losing action removes one source of evidence the loop did not select. [CLAIM-342](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md) answers it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-364](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-364.md) v2 | Low supervisory cost cannot show non-domination: processes conditioned never to object also coordinate without override, so whether an organization dominates its processes must be read from what happens when a constituent dissents, and from its history | A45's, U45 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, against the owner's non-domination criterion ([CLAIM-362](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-362.md)) read through its economy: "a system whose subordinate processes have been conditioned never to object might exhibit perfect local harmony", and "A quiet subordinate process isn't necessarily a satisfied one." It is [THEORY-040](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-040.md)'s manipulation objection, and [QUESTION-071](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-071.md), applied to the new criterion. It does not say the criterion fails, only that cost cannot certify it. The authenticity line was set aside on 2026-10-05; whether it reopens is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-393](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-393.md) | Ordinary and legal attributions of agency to an artifact cannot serve as the independent marks that would defeat the record's agency test, because they turn on whether its mechanism is understood: a known mechanism invites "This is all just programmed!", an inscrutable one invites fear, whatever the description lengths | From Boyle's "inscrutability paradox" in The Line ([LIT-1288](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1288.md), read in [NOTE-1014](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1014.md)): if an apparently general AI comes from well-understood programming, people will doubt it has autonomous consciousness, since it is "merely doing or saying that which we have programmed it to do"; if its workings are inscrutable, they will find it "more mysterious and potentially more threatening" (p. 30; pp. 54, 246, 272). [CLAIM-174](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md)'s defeater counts a test-passing factor that is "by independent marks, not an agent". For artifacts, the marks to hand, public and legal judgement, are not independent of what is known about the mechanism. The objection does not say [CLAIM-174](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md)'s test is wrong, only that this route to defeating it is not open. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-411](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-411.md) v4 | Under the broad, nonphenomenal definition of interpretation the constitutive thesis uses, substantial processing that is not independently shown to be experiential meets the definition, blindsight's apparently unconscious visual discrimination among it, so interpretation alone does not establish experience, and the thesis must say which further organizational properties, if any, make an interpretation experiential | A3's "most serious challenge" to the owner's thesis, which every later reply accepted. Once interpretation is defined broadly and without experience, as the thesis requires, it admits much processing that is not shown to be experiential: "Interpretation ⇏ Conscious experience. At least, not under an unrestricted definition of interpretation." The objection is that the thesis is incomplete, not that it is false. A7 kept it as the theory's "open sufficiency condition". The record already separates access from experience ([QUESTION-048](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-048.md), [THEORY-577](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-577.md)), and the candidate conditions the exchange named (global availability, integration, higher-order or recursive modelling, valuation, perspective) are the question [QUESTION-254](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-254.md) asks. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-419](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-419.md) | The record's grammar is fixed at any moment but amendable by decision, and in practice a move that fit no scheme or relation has been treated as a defect of the grammar and answered by amending it, so a move the grammar cannot hold is not only forced or lost; whether every such move is caught is not shown | The owner's, at U18 of the exchange of 2026-10-22: "when we've encountered representational challenges, we've generally interpreted those as a symptom of a represntational weakness of the record and used that opportunity to mature the luria configuration, featureset, or both." It answers [CLAIM-181](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md), which had no reply on file, with the record's own decisions as evidence. It narrows [CLAIM-181](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md) rather than defeating it: the record shows moves that were caught and the grammar amended, and one case ([ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)'s literature roles) where a recurring move was left in prose. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-426](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-426.md) | Where a judgement's circulation helps bring about what it says, its visibility, repetition and attributed plurality are evidence about what it will bring about, so the rule that a judgement's authority should come from its grounds and not its visibility holds for judgements of what already is, and not without qualification for judgements of what someone or something will become | The owner, on 2026-10-23, after [CLAIM-425](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-425.md) was filed: "this is reminding me of 'hyperstition'". Land's definition ([LIT-1396](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1396.md)): "hyperstitions – by their very existence as ideas – function causally to bring about their own reality." [CLAIM-425](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-425.md) says not to let a judgement's popularity substitute for its credibility. For a judgement whose popularity helps make it true, popularity is evidence, about the future it is helping to make. The claim narrows [CLAIM-425](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-425.md), it does not reverse it: visibility still does not show what was the case. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-431](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-431.md) | A corporation's functional remorse cannot be told from prudence: any procedure or role duty that makes others' harms its concern was put there for its own ends, reputation, liability or recruitment, so the line between harm as concern and harm as threat, and with it the line between a remorseful and a psychopathic corporation, does not hold, and the clinical word adds nothing to a description of its incentives | The objection to the record's reading of the "institutional psychopath", revised on 2026-10-23 when the reading was revised. The first version said the clinical word adds nothing because a corporation shows only psychopathy's conduct; once the record assigns functional affect ([CLAIM-039](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-039.md)), that premise is gone. What remains is sharper: the reading's distinction between a harm a corporation takes as its own concern (remorse) and a harm it takes only as a threat (fear) may not be drawable for a corporation, whose every concern was installed for its own ends. Velasquez's "as if" ([LIT-1432](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1432.md)) in functional form. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-438](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-438.md) | An ordering serving as the negotiation's potential, as the potential account of valence defines it, tracks 'wanting', not 'liking': sensitized incentive salience wins a system's conflicts, persists and resumes while hedonic impact measured by taste reactivity stays flat or falls, so the regime the account calls hedonic valence is motivational valence, and hedonic valence, if it is anywhere in the account, is elsewhere | Raised by the reading of Berridge and Kringelbach ([NOTE-1110](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1110.md)) filed on 2026-10-23 for the potential account. Sensitized 'wanting' meets all three of Frijda's marks of control precedence, which [TERM-076](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-076.md) uses to define potential, while 'liking' stays flat or falls. That is [CLAIM-440](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md)'s own defeater, intensity that does not track control precedence. Hesp et al. ([NOTE-1111](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1111.md)) concede the same of their account, which puts valence in the system's model of its own potential rather than in the potential. | Active |
| [CLAIM-441](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-441.md) | Flow tells against the potential account's condition that valence is undefined where no pair is contested: on the record's own account of flow nothing is overridden because an activity's immediate reward and its longer-run value coincide, yet flow is reported as positive, so either flow's positivity is intrinsic pleasantness and not goal-conduciveness valence, or flow keeps contested pairs its processes settle among themselves, or the positivity comes after the episode and not during it, or the condition is wrong | The assistant's, from the comparison of the record's will and affect lines of 2026-10-23, filed at the owner's direction. [CLAIM-162](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-162.md) explains flow as intrapersonal synchronization in [TERM-050](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-050.md)'s sense: valuations coincide, so nothing needs overriding. [TERM-076](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-076.md) makes goal-conduciveness valence undefined where no pair is contested. Together they make flow's valence undefined, while flow is reported as positive. The report is second-hand: the flow literature is registered unread ([LIT-914](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-914.md)), and that it is positive during the episode, rather than in retrospect, is exactly what is unchecked. Four exits are named; the objection holds until one is shown. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-448](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-448.md) | An ordinal potential describes only the winning-move relation it is computed on; where an organization's legibility regime selects which contests are admitted or recorded, an acyclic record, even a persistent potential, can be the product of selective contestation, so observed coherence is not evidence that the organization's perspectives are integrated, and an intervention that improves its self-governance may at first increase the disagreement observed | From the exchange of 2026-10-24 (workbench entry of 2026-10-24, U19–U21), after the owner pointed to [CASE-124](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-124.md) ("i think we already have a three variable system somewhere, where the third component is described as legibility") and asked for the synthesis to be tied back: if the legibility regime decides which objections are registered, the record of wins on which [CLAIM-440](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md) reads valence can be acyclic for the wrong reason. Objects to reading a prevailing potential as an integrated organization's valence without a check on what was admitted. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-449](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-449.md) | The potential account of valence's first consequence, no frustration, no valence, runs together two relations: perspectives' contested rankings, which a record of winning moves registers, and demands that are jointly infeasible, which the compatibility complex registers; rankings can contest while every demand is satisfiable, and demands can be infeasible before any contest is recorded, so the consequence needs one of them named, and the absorbed writer, valenced with nothing contested, tests whichever is chosen | Raised in the exchange of 2026-10-23 (workbench entry of 2026-10-24, U5), when the owner asked for "cases or theories that aren't richly connected but which may bear on questions or claims more deeply than we are giving them credit". The reply proposed "a new counterclaim against consequence 1 of [CLAIM-440](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md), explicitly distinguishing evaluative disagreement, contested efficacy, and structural frustration", grounded in the absorbed writer and the three-demand case. Filed here at the owner's request to record the exchange. | Proposed |
